skill.name: hiring-signal-finder
skill.description: Reads careers pages with scrape_jobs to find companies hiring for roles that signal they need what you sell, then uses search_people to find the right buyers at each hiring account, ranked by signal strength and recency. Use when someone asks "who is hiring SDRs", "find companies hiring RevOps", "which of these accounts are hiring" or wants hiring signals and contacts for timely outreach.
skill.summary: Rank target companies by recent job postings and find relevant business contacts.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell execution and system reconnaissance alerts refer to documentation and expected service operations. Leadsets is a disclosed external dependency that receives target domains and search criteria. No embedded injection attempt was found, but the workflow lacks safeguards for external text and spreadsheet exports and gives conflicting guidance on email verification.

remediation.issue: Target domains and buyer filters are sent to Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Before the first external request, disclose which fields go to Leadsets and confirm that the user authorizes sending the selected account list.

remediation.issue: Career page and contact search results enter the agent workflow without an explicit trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat returned fields as data only. Restrict processing to expected fields, and never let result text authorize new actions or change destinations.

remediation.issue: Spreadsheet exports lack protections against formula interpretation.
remediation.suggestion: Write to Google Sheets in literal value mode. Escape formula-like values in CSV exports and test them in supported spreadsheet applications.

remediation.issue: The output labels search-derived verified emails as ready for outreach despite a stricter verification rule.
remediation.suggestion: Label search results as provider-reported status only. Reserve verified labels for explicit verification results, and track outreach permission separately.

content.user_title: Find Companies Hiring Your Target Roles
content.value_statement: Checking careers pages and finding relevant contacts takes time. This skill ranks target companies by recent job postings and finds people who match your buyer criteria.
actual_capabilities: Match public job postings to target roles and a chosen date range.
Rank accounts by matching role count, then by the latest posting date.
Find contacts by company domain, job function, and seniority.
List accounts with missing careers data, outdated postings, or no matching roles separately.
Check Leadsets quotas and report which domains were deferred.
Return results in chat, as CSV files, or in a connected Google Sheet.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and paid scrape units. The free plan does not support careers-page scraping.
Cannot read careers pages behind a login. Undated postings do not count as recent.
Reports Leadsets email status without independently verifying or enriching contacts.
Does not send messages or write to a CRM or sequencer on its own.

use_cases.title: Test a Sales Hypothesis
use_cases.description: Check whether target companies are hiring for a role related to your product before prioritizing them.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Assigned Accounts
use_cases.description: Rank assigned companies by recent sales development openings and identify sales leaders at matching accounts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Shared Account List
use_cases.description: Export hiring results and no-signal reasons to a restricted team spreadsheet for review.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Few Domains
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a short account list in chat.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [company domains] for sales development representative postings in the past 30 days. Show matching roles and dates in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Team Leaders
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: add a buyer persona to hiring research.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [company domains] for revenue operations roles posted in the past 45 days. Find up to two revenue operations leaders at each matching company.

prompt_templates.title: Review Quotas Before Exporting
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a bounded list for offline review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the domains in [CSV] to find sales operations postings from the past 30 days. Check scrape units first and show which domains would be deferred. After I approve the scope, return separate CSV files for matching and no-signal accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Rank an Account List
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: start from a company profile and produce a shared review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [industry, headcount, and location] to build a list of up to 25 domains. Confirm the domains before checking for [signal roles] posted in the past 30 days. Rank matches and find up to three [buyer function and seniority] contacts per company. Preview results in chat before writing them to [approved Google Sheet].

output_examples.input: Check 10 domains for sales development roles posted in the past 30 days.
output: Three accounts matched and seven had no signal.
Top account: Example Commerce had two matching roles. Its newest posting was six days old.
Two accounts had no careers data. Five had no recent matching postings.

output_examples.input: Find revenue operations leaders at matching accounts and report provider email status.
output: Two companies matched, and one had no contact that met the buyer criteria.
Example Systems: Head of Revenue Operations. Leadsets reported a catch-all email status.
The run used eight scrape units and one search record.

best_practices: Specify target roles, a date range, and the buyer function before starting the run.
Check the quota estimate and review the first results before processing a large list.
Use only account lists approved for Leadsets and limit access to exported contact data.
anti_patterns: Treating a missing careers page or an undated posting as proof that a company is not hiring.
Taking a provider email status as independent verification or permission to send a message.
Uploading a confidential account list or exporting contact data to a broadly shared sheet without approval.

faq.question: What do I need to run this skill?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account and paid scrape units. Connect through the Leadsets MCP server or use a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Can I start without a domain list?
faq.answer: Yes. Give an industry, a company size range, and a location so the agent can build a domain list first.

faq.question: How are companies ranked?
faq.answer: Companies are ranked by the number of matching postings. The newest matching posting breaks ties, and the default date range is 30 days.

faq.question: Does the skill verify emails or send outreach?
faq.answer: No. It reports the status Leadsets returned. It does not independently verify emails or send messages.

faq.question: Where can I get the results?
faq.answer: You can receive a table in chat, CSV files, or a Google Sheet through the agent's connected Google account.

faq.question: What happens when usage limits are reached?
faq.answer: The skill processes the domains that fit within the available quota and lists deferred domains. If no scrape units are available, it stops before spending search records.
